panels.visual: Travelling sophists in fine robes teaching a crowd of rich young men in the Agora, each with a heavy bag of coins at his feet, confident smirks
panels.caption: Sophists travelled from city to city teaching young men to win arguments, for money.

panels.visual: Two sophists side by side with price tags hanging from their lecterns: one tag reads 100 MINAS (a huge pile of coin bags), the other reads 5 MINAS (a small bag)
panels.caption: Protagoras was said to charge a hundred minas. Evenus charged five.

panels.visual: Socrates (ugly, bald, bushy beard, barefoot, shabby cloak) holding out empty open hands with a cheerful grin, a tiny price tag showing 0 and an empty pouch
panels.caption: Socrates charged nothing, and he had nothing.

speech.speaker: Socrates
speech.text: I charged nothing, and I had nothing.

panels.visual: Socrates looking up at a very confident pompous sophist with a raised chin, a big question mark floating between them
panels.caption: He would ask a simple question.

panels.visual: The pompous sophist answers with a grand gesture and a speech scroll, young men watching, a mood of confidence
panels.caption: The sophist answered confidently.

panels.visual: Socrates with a finger raised asking another question, a chain of question marks, the sophist's smirk beginning to slip, a sweat drop
panels.caption: Then another question, and another.

panels.visual: The sophist tangled in his own words, hair standing up, eyes spinning, a knot of scribbled lines above his head, sweat drops flying; young men in the background laughing
panels.caption: Until he contradicted himself in front of everyone.

panels.visual: The Oracle at Delphi (the Pythia on a golden tripod in swirling mist) declaring in glowing light, Socrates confused in the foreground
panels.caption: The oracle called him the wisest man in Athens.

speech.speaker: Pythia
speech.text: No one is wiser than Socrates.

panels.visual: Socrates tapping his own chest with a gentle smile while behind him a row of pompous Athenians each stand with a thought bubble full of 'I know'
panels.caption: The only reason: he did not think he knew what he did not know. Everyone else did.

speech.speaker: Socrates
speech.text: I don't think I know what I don't know.

panels.visual: A general on a hillside tricking the enemy: a decoy campfire and a hidden army, the general smiling slyly; Socrates and the young Euthydemus watching in an inset
panels.caption: Is deceiving always wrong? A general who tricks the enemy?

panels.visual: A father hiding bitter medicine in a spoon of honeyed food to feed his sick son in bed, the boy trusting, the father tender
panels.caption: A father who tricks his sick son into taking medicine?

panels.visual: A sad man sitting with his head in his hands in a dim room; his friend gently lifting a sword away from the table and holding it behind his back, tender, the sad man not harmed, mood quiet and kind
panels.caption: A man who takes a desperate friend's sword away?
